# Kubernetes (EKS/On-Prem), Internal RFC1918 Subnets & Split-Horizon DNS (`onprem-k8s-network-rfc1918`)

> **Group:** II. Identity, Gateways & Multi-Cloud / On-Prem
> **Product Archetypes:** Cloud_Infra_IaC, OnPrem_Enterprise_Network
> **Trigger Signals:** kubernetes, k8s, helm, docker, container, rfc1918, 10.135, 10.133, 10.228, 10.250, vpc, subnet, onprem

## [ BLOCK: internal-dns-leak-and-vpc-colocation ]
### Split-Horizon DNS Leaks (RFC1918 10.x) & High-Blast VPC Co-Location
- Identify internal hostnames (`10.135.x.x`, `10.133.x.x`, `10.228.x.x`, `10.250.x.x`) leaked in public DNS, config files, or OpenAPI `servers[]` blocks.
- Assess co-location blast radius where critical control planes (ArgoCD, Central Auth, KMS, Core DB, Doris/Flink/Superset) share the same internal IP or K8s node without NetworkPolicy isolation.

## [ BLOCK: k8s-manifests-helm-and-service-mesh ]
### Kubernetes RBAC, Pod Security, ServiceAccount Tokens & East-West Trust
- Audit Helm charts and K8s manifests for `privileged: true`, hostPath mounts, automounted ServiceAccount tokens, and unauthenticated internal service ports (`:8000`, `:8202`).

## [ BLOCK: k8s-secrets-logging-and-container-escape ]
### Kubernetes Secret Exposure, Audit Logging & Pod-to-Node Escalation
- Check K8s manifests and ConfigMaps for plaintext credentials, database URLs, or private keys committed in git.
- Verify `NetworkPolicy` enforcement isolating internet-facing pods from internal RFC1918 control planes (`10.x.x.x`), databases, and OT gateways.

### Standard Mappings
- OWASP-API8:2023, ASVS-5.0-V13-Configuration, ASVS-5.0-V14-Data-Protection, ASVS-5.0-V16-Security-Logging-and-Error-Handling, IEC-62443-4-2, CWE-250, CWE-668

### Safe Patterns (Refutation Anchors)
- Kubernetes Pod securityContext with runAsNonRoot: true, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, capabilities: { drop: ["ALL"] }, and automountServiceAccountToken: false
- Default-deny Kubernetes NetworkPolicies restricting east-west pod traffic to explicit service ports/namespaces plus Istio/Linkerd PeerAuthentication mtls.mode: STRICT
- Secrets injected via External Secrets Operator / HashiCorp Vault / AWS KMS rather than plaintext Helm values.yaml or ConfigMaps
- Dedicated namespace-scoped Role/RoleBinding granting only read access to specific ConfigMaps without cluster-wide secrets or pods/exec verbs
- Split-horizon DNS isolating internal RFC1918 control plane records (10.135.x.x, 10.133.x.x, 10.228.x.x, 10.250.x.x) onto private Route53/CoreDNS zones unreachable from public resolvers
- Structured JSON audit logging scrubbing Authorization headers, JWTs, database passwords, and PII before shipping to Elastic/Loki/Splunk

### Vulnerable Patterns
- Containers running with securityContext.privileged: true, hostNetwork: true, hostPID: true, or mounting /var/run/docker.sock or hostPath: /
- ClusterRoleBinding granting cluster-admin or wildcard resources: ["secrets", "pods/exec", "*"] to default application ServiceAccounts
- Internal RFC1918 IPs (10.135.x.x, 10.133.x.x, 10.228.x.x, 10.250.x.x) and unauthenticated gRPC/HTTP internal service ports exposed in public DNS or OpenAPI servers[] blocks
- Plaintext database credentials, private keys, or API tokens committed directly in Helm values.yaml, k8s ConfigMaps, or docker-compose.yml
- Flat Kubernetes cluster network without NetworkPolicy isolation allowing a compromised DMZ web pod to connect directly to core databases, ArgoCD, or OT gateways
- Application error handlers returning raw stack traces, SQL queries, or environment dumps in HTTP 500 responses or writing unredacted tokens to stdout logs

### Mandatory Evidence (`required_evidence`)
- ev_... excerpt of Kubernetes Deployment/Pod/Helm chart manifests showing securityContext, volumes, and ServiceAccount configuration
- ev_... excerpt of Role/ClusterRole and RoleBinding/ClusterRoleBinding YAML definitions
- ev_... excerpt of NetworkPolicy, Istio PeerAuthentication/AuthorizationPolicy, or Ingress/Service definitions
- ev_... excerpt of ConfigMap, Helm values.yaml, OpenAPI servers[], or logging middleware configuration

### Verification Questions When Static Code Is Inconclusive (`questions_when_unclear`)
- Are Pod Security Standards (Restricted) or Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper admission policies enforced at the cluster level?
- Do VPC security groups or hardware firewalls segment the 10.x subnets between DMZ, production data plane, and OT zones?
- Is a service mesh (Istio/Linkerd/Cilium) enforcing strict mTLS and L7 authorization policies across all east-west pod traffic?
- Are Kubernetes Secrets encrypted at rest in etcd using an external KMS provider and injected at runtime via CSI Secrets Store?
